note: The opening chain (GDD 4.2, Spec 14.1 and 18.8), played in order. Money is in pounds. Start £150; the chain pays £460 and fitting costs £90, so you reach the van £80 short. earn (Boss, 28 Oct 2026): while you're short of a step's money, the tutorial markers point to these maps' equipment to earn it instead (the shift benches) and back to the step once you have it. markVan: until that flag is set (the first time you get in the van), the markers point to the van.

steps.journal: Your 50cc won't start. Go and see the town's mechanic at Phoenix MX on the high street.
Fit the top end at the garage workbench. Bench time costs £90.
steps.confirm: Pay £90 for bench time and fit the top end?

steps.journal: Your bike runs. Tell Paul at Phoenix MX.
Collect the garage's parts order from Moto78, the bike shop up the road.
Take the parts order back to Paul at Phoenix MX.
Service both customer bikes on the stands in the garage.
Both bikes are done. Tell Paul at Phoenix MX.
Pick up a pair of tyres from Lee Stocky at Lee's T's & Wheels.
Fit the new tyres on the tyre machine in the garage.
Tyres fitted. Tell Paul at Phoenix MX.
Take the worn cylinder to the engine rebuilder in the Industrial Zone.
Bring the rebored cylinder back to Paul at Phoenix MX.
Go and see Jedrick at Nicholls Used Motors about getting to the tracks.
Report back to Paul at Phoenix MX.
steps.toast: Everyone in town has time for you now.

steps.journal: Buy the used motor for £600. Shifts at the fabrication shop or engine rebuilder will cover the gap.
Load your bike, spares and tools into the motor. Your spares are in the chest in your rented room.
steps.toast: The motor's loaded. Ask the local champion outside Phoenix MX where to race.

steps.journal: Ask the local champion outside Phoenix MX where to race.
steps.toast: The roadworks are finished and the west road to the tracks is open.

done: Free roam: race at Farmland MX, practise on the backyard loop, or work shifts for money.

after.text: Pop into Phoenix MX. Paul has some advice about looking after your bike.
See the fabrication shop boss in the Industrial Zone. There's a troublemaker by the practice yard.
Race at Farmland MX: sign on with Joseph Halden, whose family runs all the tracks, at the race office. Your first race is free.
Finish both motos of a race day at Farmland MX. Practise on the backyard loop behind your rented room.
Win the Local Champion Championship for the Area 1 badge: enter at any track's race office, under Championships.
You hold the Area 1 badge. Win the Area 1 Championship (6 rounds, enter at any race office) for your 65cc and the road to Mountain Town.
Area 1 champion! Collect your 65cc from Bill at Moto78: take the champion's sponsor's bike, or buy a stock one. You'll need Rider Ability 10 to ride it.
Mountain Town: win the Local Champion Championship for the Area 2 badge. Enter at any Mountain Town race office.
You hold the Area 2 badge. Win the Area 2 Championship (6 rounds) for your 85cc and the road to Area 3.
Area 2 champion! Collect your 85cc small wheel from Bill at Moto78 in Home Town. You'll need Rider Ability 20 to ride it.

steps.journal: Mountain Town. Find Manny Festo, up by the top field, for the news.
See Paul at Phoenix MX, Mountain Town, about what's new in town.
Take the parts order up to Lee at Lee's T's & Wheels.
Call in at the Wheel works and meet the boss.
See the coach at the town gym.
Meet Cal Mercer, the Local Champion, by the practice yard.
steps.toast: Mountain Town's tracks are open: Clayhill MX, Valley Arena and Bog End Enduro.
